## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Gūthapāṇajātaka* (Ja 227) is a story included in the Pali Jātaka collection. Its frame story (*paccuppannavatthu*) is set at Jetavana, where the Buddha relates the account concerning a certain monk [Fausböll 1879]. The narrative tells of an intoxicated dung beetle who foolishly challenges a rutting elephant to a duel, opening with the verse *Sūro sūrena saṅgamma* ("A hero comes together in battle with a strong, fierce hero") [Appleton 2010; Fausböll 1879]. The tale serves to illustrate the perils of intoxication, whether brought about by alcohol or lust [Appleton 2010].

A notable narrative feature of the jātaka is the Bodhisatta's role: he does not appear or participate in the events of the past story (*atītavatthu*) itself, but is identified in the conclusion (*samodhāna*) as a silent tree sprite (*nivutthadevatā*) who merely observed the confrontation from the forest grove [Appleton 2010; Fausböll 1879]. In modern comparative scholarship, Naomi Appleton notes that Merlin Peris identified Greek fable motifs in the story, arguing for potential Aesopic influence [Appleton 2010].

 Automated text-matching by DharmaNexus detects no Pali-internal text reuse and finds only low-confidence alignments with Tibetan canonical literature (BO_K01_D0001-4_H0001-4) [DharmaNexus].
